title: Enhancing Small Message Aggregation with Directive-Based Deferred Execution
problem: Applications using OpenSHMEM message aggregation must explicitly manage dependencies between aggregated remote memory accesses and their subsequent uses, preventing transparent abstraction of this coordination.
motivation: Automating dependency management in message aggregation can simplify application code and improve performance in distributed memory systems.
method: The approach introduces compiler directives that automatically defer execution of code blocks until aggregated messages complete. The runtime system handles synchronization and coordination, shifting the dependency management burden from applications to the implementation.
key_novelty: Directive-based automatic deferral of code execution for managing dependencies on aggregated remote memory operations in PGAS systems.
contributions: Directive-based approach for automatic deferred execution of code dependent on aggregated messages
Preservation of algorithmic intent through abstraction of dependency management complexity
Runtime system for efficient coordination of aggregated communication and dependent operations
Demonstration on bale 3.0 classic suite applications on Frontier supercomputer
limitations: Paper limitations not discussed in abstract.
primary_theme: Directive-based deferred execution for message aggregation
